answers.why: Israel is explicitly called God's people whom the coming ruler will shepherd.
Jesus compares the centurion's faith with faith found among Israel.
The crowds say such a miracle has never been seen among Israel.
The healed crowds glorify the God of the nation Israel.
The command 'Hear, O Israel' addresses the nation concerning our God.
God helps Israel collectively as his servant in fulfillment of mercy promised to Abraham and his seed.
The God of Israel has visited and redeemed his people.
John grows up until his public manifestation to Israel.
Simeon awaits Israel's consolation through the coming Messiah.
Israel is explicitly identified as God's people alongside the Gentiles.
The child will cause the fall and rising of many people within Israel.
Israel is the nation where many widows lived during Elijah's famine.
Israel contains many lepers in Elisha's time and is contrasted with Naaman the Syrian.
